claim_boundary.note: This run establishes that one parameterised RTL block computes the reference's blockwise maximum, bit for bit, on two simulators, at one block per cycle, for seven elaborated shapes, and that it fails closed on every refusal it defines.  It establishes nothing about the block inside the engine array, nothing about the rest of the candidate pool, and nothing physical: BLOCK_MAX is not reachable from a descriptor in this run, and the frequency claim in the module header is an intent about the pipeline structure, not a measurement -- WP-M's routed record is the measurement.

cases.name: full_blocks
cases.note: three rows whose length is a whole number of blocks, random codes

cases.name: partial_final_block
cases.note: rows whose length is not a multiple of BLOCK: the final block is reduced over its real positions and the tail is never dropped

cases.name: all_negative
cases.note: a row in which every score is negative, including negative infinity: a zero pad would win here and the reference's negative-infinity pad does not

cases.name: all_padding_value
cases.note: a row of negative infinity only: every block score is negative infinity

cases.name: max_at_each_lane
cases.note: one row per lane, the maximum on that lane only: every leaf of the tree is shown to reach the result

cases.name: signed_zero
cases.note: every arrangement of negative and positive zero in a block, up to the block width: max(-0.0, +0.0) is +0.0 and max(-0.0, -0.0) is -0.0

cases.name: class_boundaries
cases.note: rotations of the format's class boundaries: zeros, least and greatest subnormal, least normal, one, greatest finite, both infinities

cases.name: ties
cases.note: blocks whose scores are all equal, at several codes: the winning code is that code, and a tie needs no tie-break

cases.name: idle_between_blocks
cases.note: the same shape as full_blocks with three idle cycles between blocks: the per-block latency is unchanged by a gap in the stream

cases.name: nan_on_padding_lane
cases.note: a partial final block whose padding lanes carry a NaN: padding lanes are never inspected, so the block retires and the result is the reference's

cases.name: rate_stream
cases.note: one row of 256 blocks driven back to back: initiation interval 1

cases.name: valid_count_zero
cases.note: an extent of zero is refused: the reference emits ceil(N / BLOCK) blocks and never an all-padding block

cases.name: valid_count_over_block
cases.note: an extent above BLOCK is refused rather than truncated into a legal one

cases.name: partial_not_row_last
cases.note: a short block that is not row-last is refused: only a final block is partial under the reference, and accepting an interior short block would shift every block index after it

cases.name: nan_on_real_lane
cases.note: a NaN on a real lane is refused: the order is not total on NaNs

cases.name: row_bound
cases.note: a row of exactly MAX_BLOCKS = 2048 blocks retires, and the block after it is refused with DETAIL_BLOCK_MAX_ROW_BLOCKS

cases.name: after_clear
cases.note: a plain row after every refusal case: clear restores the block and the row's block index restarts at zero

cases.name: full_blocks
cases.note: three rows whose length is a whole number of blocks, random codes

cases.name: partial_final_block
cases.note: rows whose length is not a multiple of BLOCK: the final block is reduced over its real positions and the tail is never dropped

cases.name: all_negative
cases.note: a row in which every score is negative, including negative infinity: a zero pad would win here and the reference's negative-infinity pad does not

cases.name: all_padding_value
cases.note: a row of negative infinity only: every block score is negative infinity

cases.name: max_at_each_lane
cases.note: one row per lane, the maximum on that lane only: every leaf of the tree is shown to reach the result

cases.name: signed_zero
cases.note: every arrangement of negative and positive zero in a block, up to the block width: max(-0.0, +0.0) is +0.0 and max(-0.0, -0.0) is -0.0

cases.name: class_boundaries
cases.note: rotations of the format's class boundaries: zeros, least and greatest subnormal, least normal, one, greatest finite, both infinities

cases.name: ties
cases.note: blocks whose scores are all equal, at several codes: the winning code is that code, and a tie needs no tie-break

cases.name: idle_between_blocks
cases.note: the same shape as full_blocks with three idle cycles between blocks: the per-block latency is unchanged by a gap in the stream

cases.name: nan_on_padding_lane
cases.note: a partial final block whose padding lanes carry a NaN: padding lanes are never inspected, so the block retires and the result is the reference's

cases.name: rate_stream
cases.note: one row of 64 blocks driven back to back: initiation interval 1

cases.name: valid_count_zero
cases.note: an extent of zero is refused: the reference emits ceil(N / BLOCK) blocks and never an all-padding block

cases.name: valid_count_over_block
cases.note: an extent above BLOCK is refused rather than truncated into a legal one

cases.name: partial_not_row_last
cases.note: a short block that is not row-last is refused: only a final block is partial under the reference, and accepting an interior short block would shift every block index after it

cases.name: nan_on_real_lane
cases.note: a NaN on a real lane is refused: the order is not total on NaNs

cases.name: row_bound
cases.note: a row of exactly MAX_BLOCKS = 64 blocks retires, and the block after it is refused with DETAIL_BLOCK_MAX_ROW_BLOCKS

cases.name: after_clear
cases.note: a plain row after every refusal case: clear restores the block and the row's block index restarts at zero
